tool.name: apply-hardening
tool.description: Applies one protection. A reversible protection is applied directly and the answer carries the handle that puts it back. confirmation.description: The single-use confirmation a person minted for a proposal. Required only for a protection whose way back is not guaranteed by the undo ledger alone.

abilities.label: Change the script and content policy

tool.description: Either starts enforcing the script and content policy under test (change: enforce), which can stop checkout or other pages loading something they need, or allows one source the policy reported (change: allow_source, with directive and source from get-fix-targets for csp_report_only), which widens it. Enforcing is taken back on the site; an allowed source is taken off with remove-script-source. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

tool.name: deactivate-plugin

tool.name: end-sessions
tool.description: Ends sessions for one user_id or scope site, only for accounts this administrator may edit. The plan names the reach, skipped accounts, network-wide effects and the administrator’s own browser sessions. Ended sessions cannot be restored. Requires the proposal and its single-use confirmation after the person agrees. There is no direct execution path.

tool.name: enter-lockdown
tool.description: Pauses every assistant connection, including the caller, ends dashboard-capable sessions within the stated bound, and leaves the front end and checkout untouched. tool.name: get-hub-link
tool.description: Whether this site sends its security events and a heartbeat to BetterShield Hub, signed: the public key the hub checks them against, the id the site signs as, and which kinds of events it sends. Off, the key and the id are empty: the link is off, or this is a copy at another address or a staging copy, or the site is not connected to hub.bettershield.ai. Pass the hub’s nonce (32 bytes, base64url) as challenge to get proof: the key’s Ed25519 signature, base64url, over five lines joined by a newline: “bettershield hub link proof v1”, https://hub.bettershield.ai, this site’s home URL without a trailing slash, the site id and the challenge. cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, to read the changes past the ones it carried.

list.description: Which changes to list: the open ones (the default), or the accepted ones (expected). A cursor belongs to the list that gave it.

monitoring_active.description: True when a file check has finished within two of its own scheduled intervals; false on a site whose checks have stopped.

next_check_at.description: The next scheduled check, or empty when the appointment on record has already passed.

missed_check_at.description: The appointment that has passed without being kept, or empty. Empty in both fields means no check is scheduled.

changes_truncated.description: True when open_changes exceeds what this list carries.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as cursor to read the next page of changes. Empty when this page is the last.

changes_error.description: Why the change list could not be read. Empty when it was read. When set, changes is what could be gathered and changes_truncated says nothing about paging.

progress.description: How far a running check has got: which target of how many, the pass it is on, files compared so far and what is being checked now. Zeros when none is running.

confirmation.description: The single-use confirmation apply takes, present only when confirm_by is "conversation". Show the plan to the person and send this only after they agree; it expires with the plan.

abilities.label: Move a downloadable file into quarantine

tool.name: quarantine-exposed-file
tool.description: Moves one leftover tool, backup, dump or log that visitors can download into quarantine. Name a path get-fix-targets lists for leftover_tools_reachable or artifacts_downloadable. A moved file is put back from the quarantine list on the site. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

annotations.title: Move a downloadable file into quarantine

abilities.label: Move an unused plugin or theme into quarantine

tool.name: quarantine-extension
tool.description: Moves one deactivated plugin or unused theme get-fix-targets lists for inactive_extensions into quarantine, out of visitors’ reach. It is not running, so the site behaves as before. Putting it back takes a plan from propose-fix-undo. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

annotations.title: Move an unused plugin or theme into quarantine

tool.name: query-activity
tool.description: A bounded, paginated window over the activity log. Retention limits are applied silently and reported in the response.

since.description: ISO 8601 UTC. Clamped to the retention limit.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

sites.description: Site ids on a network. Honored only for a caller who may read the whole network; otherwise the call answers for the current site.

tool.name: query-agent-activity
tool.description: A bounded, paginated window over Abilities API invocations on this site, whoever registered the ability. Inputs are recorded as digests and never returned. Retention limits are applied silently and reported in the response.

outcome.description: Narrow to one outcome. permission_denied is the one worth watching.

namespace.description: The ability name's namespace prefix. This is a naming convention, not an enforced link to the plugin that registered it.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

user_label.description: A display label for the account, resolved when the row is read. Never a stored user record.

input_digest.description: A keyed SHA-256 of the normalized input. Never the input itself.

abilities.label: Apply a protection that stopped working again

tool.name: reapply-protection
tool.description: Applies one protection that is on but reads as not working again, with the settings it already has. Only a protection get-fix-targets lists for hardening_not_working. A protection that changes how people sign in or the site’s address is applied again on the site. Name the target to apply it now. To apply a plan from propose-finding-fix, send that plan’s proposal_id and confirmation, with its state_digest if you have it, and no target.

annotations.title: Apply a protection that stopped working again

tool.name: recheck-finding
tool.description: Asks one finding whose cause is outside this plugin, or the domain’s mail and certificate records, to be checked again. A certificate or records lookup is queued and answers later. Changes nothing on the site.

abilities.label: Compare one plugin’s changed files again

tool.name: recheck-package
tool.description: Compares one plugin’s open file changes against the copy wordpress.org published for the installed version, and closes each that matches now, as after an update finished. Bounded: pass the returned after to carry on while left is above zero. Changes no file.

annotations.title: Compare one plugin’s changed files again

tool.name: refresh-incidents
tool.description: Runs one bounded pass correlating existing evidence and returns whether more work is pending. Changes no protection and applies no incident response.

tool.name: remove-scheduled-events
tool.description: Removes every scheduled run of the named hooks, which nothing on the site answers now. Name hooks get-fix-targets lists for cron_events_unanswered, in one call. The runs are kept in the undo record first; putting them back takes a plan from propose-fix-undo. Name the target to apply it now. To apply a plan from propose-finding-fix, send that plan’s proposal_id and confirmation, with its state_digest if you have it, and no target.

abilities.label: Take a source off the script and content policy

tool.name: remove-script-source
tool.description: Takes one allowed source off the test script and content policy, so the policy reports it again. This narrows the policy. Allowing it again takes a plan from propose-script-policy. Name the target to apply it now. To apply a plan from propose-finding-fix, send that plan’s proposal_id and confirmation, with its state_digest if you have it, and no target.

annotations.title: Take a source off the script and content policy

tool.name: rename-admin-account
tool.description: Gives the account whose username is "admin" a new username. That person signs in with the new one from then on. Behind a recovery link verified within the day, and never the account the assistant acts as. Renaming it back takes a plan from propose-fix-undo. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

tool.name: restore-file
tool.description: Puts the published copy of one changed file back, once, with the confirmation for the plan propose-file-restore returned. The file as it is now goes to quarantine first, the published copy is checked against its checksum before it is used, and the answer carries the handle revert-hardening takes to put the current file back. That way back is best effort, not guaranteed, which is why this waits for the person’s agreement.

tool.name: revert-hardening
tool.description: Restores what a change made through these abilities replaced, using the handle it returned. A plugin switched back on and a restored file put back are the safe direction and ask for nothing more. Taking a protection off is not the safe direction, whatever put it there: for that, ask propose-hardening with action "revert", show the person the plan, and send the confirmation it carries. A finding fix’s handle (scheduled events, a REST route, a folder, a plugin update or quarantine, an account change) takes its plan from propose-fix-undo the same way.

confirmation.description: The single-use confirmation a person minted for a revert plan. Required when the handle names a protection; ignored for a plugin switched back on or a file put back.

tool.name: revoke-app
tool.description: Revokes another connected app’s access and refresh credentials. Refuses the calling app. Reconnecting needs a new approval on the site; revoked credentials cannot be restored. Requires the proposal and its single-use confirmation after the person agrees. There is no direct execution path.

tool.name: revoke-app-password
tool.description: Revokes one application password nobody has used for a long time. Name the key get-fix-targets lists for application_passwords_stale. A revoked password cannot be restored, and the credential the caller uses is never revoked here. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

tool.name: run-audit
tool.description: Runs the site’s security audit and returns its Overview. Changes no protection. Requires write access and uses its own hourly allowance.

abilities.label: Check part of the site’s files

tool.name: run-file-check
tool.description: Starts or continues one bounded slice of the file check. A running result needs further slices; the answer names the next scheduled check when one exists. Slices that continue a check under way have their own, larger hourly allowance. Changes no file or protection.

annotations.title: Check part of the site’s files

tool.name: run-recovery-check
tool.description: Verifies the site’s existing recovery setup and returns its readiness. At most once a minute. Never creates a recovery link or recovery codes and never accepts a caller’s claim that recovery is ready.

abilities.label: Run the site’s overdue scheduled work

tool.name: run-scheduled-work
tool.description: Asks the site to run the scheduled work it has fallen behind on, once, inside the runner’s own claim. Answers with how far behind it is. Changes no protection.

annotations.title: Run the site’s overdue scheduled work

tool.name: run-vulnerability-check
tool.description: Compares the installed plugins, themes and WordPress against the vulnerability feed now rather than at the next daily run, then refreshes the findings. Read get-vulnerability-state for the result. Changes no code or protection.

tool.name: set-incident-status
tool.description: Acknowledges one incident directly with incident_id and status acknowledged, or applies a confirmed proposal with proposal_id and confirmation. Handling requires a proposal because it stops evidence collection; its undo reopens the incident as acknowledged.

tool.name: stop-ignoring-file
tool.description: Reports one accepted file change again, including a change marked from the site dashboard. Requires write access but no confirmation. Changes no file bytes.

tool.name: suspend-account
tool.description: Suspends one privileged account get-fix-targets lists for privileged_account_dormant, so it cannot sign in. Never the acting account, the last administrator, or an account recovery or alerts go to. Letting it back in takes a plan from propose-fix-undo. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.

tool.name: update-plugin
tool.description: Updates one plugin to the newer version wordpress.org offers, keeping the current version so it can be put back. Name a plugin file get-fix-targets lists for plugin_updates_available or vulnerabilities_known. New code can break a site in ways putting the old version back does not fully reverse, so this is always a plan a person agrees to. Show the plan to the person and execute only after they agree, using its single-use confirmation. No direct execution path is offered.
